title: Inventory cost flow & valuation — Brook Outdoor Gear
instructions: Brook Outdoor Gear sells one model of camp stove and uses a **periodic** system. Compute inventory under each method, then evaluate the year-end valuation memo.

exhibits.title: Stove activity for the year
exhibits.content:
| Date | Units | Unit cost |
|---|---:|---:|
| Beginning inventory | 400 | $15 |
| April purchase | 600 | $16 |
| July purchase | 500 | $18 |
| October purchase | 300 | $19 |

Units sold during the year: **1,350**.

exhibits.title: Year-end market data
exhibits.content: Expected selling price per stove: **$20**. Expected costs to sell per stove: **$3.50**. Current replacement cost: **$16.20**. Normal profit margin: **$2.00** per stove.

rows.label: Cost of goods available for sale

parts.prompt: Answer the valuation questions. NRV per unit = 20.00 − 3.50 = 16.50.

rows.label: If Brook uses FIFO, the year-end carrying amount per unit is…
rows.explanation: FIFO → lower of cost and NRV. FIFO unit cost = 8,400 ÷ 450 = 18.67 > NRV 16.50 → write down to **$16.50**.

rows.label: If Brook uses LIFO, market per unit is…
rows.explanation: Ceiling 16.50; floor 16.50 − 2.00 = 14.50; replacement 16.20 is in between → market 16.20.

rows.label: Under LIFO, is a write-down required?
rows.explanation: LIFO unit cost = 6,800 ÷ 450 = 15.11 < market 16.20 → no write-down.

parts.prompt: Review the controller's draft memo and correct any errors.

segments.text: Because prices rose during the year,

segments.original: LIFO reports lower cost of goods sold than FIFO
options: LIFO reports lower cost of goods sold than FIFO
LIFO reports higher cost of goods sold than FIFO
LIFO and FIFO report the same cost of goods sold
segments.answer: LIFO reports higher cost of goods sold than FIFO
segments.explanation: With rising prices LIFO expenses the newest, highest costs (23,500 vs. FIFO 21,900).

segments.text: . If we adopt LIFO for tax purposes, we

segments.original: may continue to use FIFO in our financial statements
options: may continue to use FIFO in our financial statements
must also use LIFO in our financial statements
segments.answer: must also use LIFO in our financial statements
segments.explanation: The LIFO conformity rule requires LIFO for book purposes when used for tax.

segments.text: . Any FIFO write-down to net realizable value

segments.original: may not be reversed in later years even if prices recover
options: may not be reversed in later years even if prices recover
must be reversed when prices recover
is recorded in other comprehensive income
segments.answer: may not be reversed in later years even if prices recover
segments.explanation: Correct as written: under U.S. GAAP the written-down amount becomes the new cost basis.
